summary.intent: Write a structured implementation plan for adding keyword editing, threshold configuration, and related features to the memory-loop system in the superset CLI project.
summary.outcome: A complete plan file was written to docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-03-memory-loop-edit-keywords-threshold.md covering 13 tasks, self-reviewed for spec coverage and type consistency, then committed (with force-add to bypass gitignore).

repo: Plan files live under docs/superpowers/plans/ and are gitignored by default, requiring force-add to commit them.
The memory-loop injection scoring uses a 3x multiplier for keyword phrase matches via countMatchedKeywords.
GenerationThreshold uses a tri-state singleton pattern (passesEvidenceGate) rather than a simple boolean.
Keyword display appears on the TUI detail page; threshold config appears on the TUI settings tab as a card with an override indicator (e.g., 'balanced*').
ResolveGenerationThreshold handles preset validation and override resolution.
RefreshHistory is extended to carry threshold info alongside existing history metadata.
CLI threshold and edit subcommands are grouped under the same Task 9 (memory CLI surface).
workflow: Self-review process included: spec coverage check (every spec item mapped to a task), placeholder scan (no TBDs/TODOs), and type consistency check (every new type traced across all tasks that reference it).
Minor display enhancements (prompt tester keyword line) can be folded into the task that introduces the underlying data structure rather than creating a separate task.
Gitignored plan/doc files need explicit force-add before committing.

friction: Plan docs are gitignored, requiring a separate force-add step to commit them — a minor but recurring annoyance.
open_items: Score visibility in the prompt tester (keyword match count line) was noted as not explicitly tasked but deemed covered implicitly by the reason-string update in Task 2 — worth verifying during implementation.
Accessible mode handling for the edit TUI wizard (huh forms fallback) is mentioned in Task 11 but details are not fully elaborated.
